content.text: {"utterance":"Leonie, take your poem. Someone can recite it flawlessly next week and still not be able to do anything with it: change the meter, spot a line that has been swapped, say why a stanza ends where it does. Recipe version: I'd say someone has learned risotto when the saffron runs out and they swap in something else and adjust the stock and timing. A perfect recital of the recipe tells me nothing about that. Still, you're right that I can't just call any success learning; a lucky substitution shouldn't count unless it repeats.","cites":["NI3"],"memory":"Claim: learning is using something in a genuinely new situation, not just recall. Concede luck needs repetition. Live question: what makes a situation new rather than a disguised repeat, and how would Leonie test poem use?"}
